Most people think the plank is a simple core exercise but poor plank mechanics can place unnecessary stress on the lower back and spine. In this video, we break down the key technique cues that help you perform a plank with proper core engagement, glute activation, and spinal alignment.

If you're an athlete, active adult, or someone dealing with low back discomfort, learning proper core stabilization mechanics is essential. Correct plank form improves trunk stability, force transfer, and injury resilience, which are critical for strength training, athletic performance, and rehabilitation.

In this video you’ll learn:
• Proper plank setup and body alignment
• How to activate your glutes and abdominal wall correctly
• The most common plank mistakes that stress the lower back
• How to maintain a stable neutral spine position

This approach reflects principles used in strength and conditioning, rehab training, and sports biomechanics to improve movement efficiency and reduce injury risk.
